To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data are consistent with the hypothesis that the signal observed in the NaI(T1)-based detector is due to WIMPs, and that this hypothesis is not excluded by the present experimental sensitivity.

(1) the DAMA collaboration has been the first to report the observation of the annual modulation signature in the rate of nuclear recoil events in the energy interval (2-6 keV) at 6.3 +/- 0.5 sigma CL, (2) the observed effect is compatible with the one expected from WIMP annual modulation signal and is incompatible with any known systematic effect, (3) the modulation phase is in agreement with that expected from WIMP interaction with the detector material,

the annual modulation signature has been detected with a high statistical significance, the WIMP mass is in the range 0.5-1.1 TeV and the cross section on NaI is in the range (0.4-1.2)x10(-6) pb, with the best fit value at (7.7+/-2.2)x10 (-6) pb, at 90% C.L.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of rare events in particle physics and astrophysics, with particular emphasis on particle dark matter and neutrino physics.
a wide spectrum of rare event searches, from the investigation of the nature and the properties of the Dark Matter particles to other rare event phenomena.
a variety of rare event searches, including the search for Dark Matter, solar neutrinos and other rare processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DAMA result is not in conflict with any other experiment and it is not excluded by any other experiment.

, in the light of present data, a WIMP component in the galactic dark halo cannot be excluded. (orig.) , after more than ten years of research activity, the DAMA experiment is still one of the most sensitive direct detection experiment in the field of particle Dark Matter searches.

the DAMA experiment, after more than 10 years of data taking and with a total exposure of 5.4x10(exp 5) kgxday, has reached a level of sensitivity to WIMPs of the order of a few times 10(exp -27) cm(exp 2) and has achieved the highest sensitivity in the field.

, in the last years, DAMA has obtained the most stringent model independent results on the WIMP search, in particular in the low mass region, and has also provided the first evidence for the WIMP annual modulating signal, which is now being investigated in detail.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DAMA experiment has been able to show that the annual modulation signal observed in the NaI(T1)-based detector set-up is compatible with the presence of Dark Matter in the Galaxy.
the modulation effect observed in DAMA is not due to seasonal variations in the environmental radioactivity.

the DAMA experiment has reached the sensitivity to exclude the hypothesis of a WIMP annual modulation signal with an amplitude larger than the one observed in the DAMA experiment, with a high level of statistical significance.
